questions.text: The device already stops (relays off, 'battery empty' message) when the batteries fall to 2.0 V. Should the Wi-Fi still be guaranteed to work below that, down to fully drained cells (1.8 V)?
options: (recommended) No: guarantee full operation down to the 2.0 V cut-off, with Wi-Fi bursts of up to 350 mA (the chip's real maximum is 335 mA). Keeps the small capacitors and the 1-year battery budget
Yes, down to 1.8 V: needs larger capacitors (about 11 mF, longer parts on the back of the board), and the sleep current goes about 1 uA over its budget (battery life about 1 % shorter)
questions.why: R3 asks for 1.8-3.4 V and 0-400 mA; R23 stops the device at 2.0 V. At 1.8 V with worst-case boost figures, 2 x 4700 uF reaches only 92 % Monte Carlo yield and pushes the R6 sleep floor to 25.6 uA (limit 25).

questions.text: Lithium AAA cells (e.g. Energizer Ultimate Lithium) give a higher voltage that can stress the Wi-Fi chip and the relays. What should we do?
options: (recommended) Label the battery cover 'alkaline or NiMH rechargeable only'; the firmware also refuses to switch the relays if the voltage is too high. No cost
Support lithium cells too: needs an extra voltage-limiting part, about +0.3 USD and a little board space
questions.why: Two fresh lithium AAA cells give about 3.6 V, which equals the ESP32-C3 absolute maximum and is above the R3 3.4 V limit.

questions.text: The two temperature-probe cables share the wall box with the 230 V wires. How should they be protected?
options: (recommended) Order probes with 300/500 V rated cable insulation (or a sleeve over the probe cable inside the box), and use a small screw terminal the installer can wire instead of a tiny crimp connector: about +0.5 USD per unit, a few mm more board edge
Keep the thin probe cables and the tiny crimp connector, and route them away from the 230 V wires by hand: no cost, but the reinforced isolation then depends on the installer
questions.why: Wiring rules (IEC 60364-5-52 / CEI 64-8) need insulation rated for the highest voltage in the box or a partition; a thin NTC cable touching a 230 V wire bypasses the board's reinforced isolation. The 1 mm crimp connector cannot be fitted by an installer.

questions.text: The prototype cost estimate is about 37.5 USD per unit (range 32-42), above the 27-28 USD accepted earlier. About 13 USD of it is one-off order costs (assembly setup, special-part fees, hand soldering of the relays, shipping) shared by only 10 units; the relays are 10 USD. What do we do?
options: (recommended) Accept about 33-38 USD for the 10 prototypes; the one-off costs fall with volume and 25 USD stays the production target
Count the probes and shipping outside the unit price: about 32 USD
Hand-solder the relays and through-hole parts in-house and order single-side assembly: saves about 2-3 USD per unit, more manual work
questions.why: Conflict C11, notes/parts.md section 2; none of the options changes the circuit.
